name: Fast food and QSR chains

problems.words: Franchisees don't share real sales, I only see what they report
quick_ideas: Ask every franchisee for the same few numbers on a fixed day, so reports can at least be compared
Visit one franchised branch at peak and compare what you see with what they report.

workzap_build.text: and integration — a multi-branch dashboard pulling POS data from every outlet, including franchisees on other systems, by hour and channel every day.

problems.ask_first: Are the franchised branches on the same POS as your own?
problems.free_stops: How each POS is connected and what franchisees must share is set out in the solution document.

problems.words: Peak hour ticket times go too long and people walk out
quick_ideas: Watch one peak and note where orders wait longest, because the fix depends on whether it's ordering, kitchen or handover
Put one crew member only on handover at peak, so finished food doesn't sit.

workzap_build.text: a ticket-time tracker from order to handover, measured every hour at every branch, showing where and when speed drops.

problems.ask_first: Where does the line slow down most — ordering, kitchen or handover?
problems.free_stops: The station layout and peak staffing plan per branch stays for the solution document.

problems.words: Each branch's burger looks different, the franchise ones are worst
quick_ideas: Put a photo of the correct build at each assembly station, so crew copy the same picture
Ask each branch to send a photo of one finished item, so you see the difference yourself.

workzap_build.text: a recipe and portion library sent to outlets with acknowledgement, and scored branch checks with photos every visit, compared across branches.

problems.ask_first: Which item varies most between branches?
problems.free_stops: The standards library and the scoring of branch checks are kept for the solution document.

problems.words: Commissary sends the wrong quantities — one branch runs out of buns while another throws them
quick_ideas: Have each branch count what arrives and sign the dispatch note, so differences are caught on the day
Ask branches to order by a fixed time each evening, so the commissary isn't guessing.

workzap_build.text: branch orders against par levels, dispatch notes and receiving confirmation on phone, with any sent-not-received gap flagged automatically.

problems.ask_first: Who decides how much each branch receives from the commissary?
problems.free_stops: Par levels per branch and the order-to-dispatch flow are detailed in the solution document.

problems.words: Cashiers apply staff discount or deal codes for friends, and refunds happen without a manager
quick_ideas: Limit discounts and refunds to manager logins, so each one has an approver
Read yesterday's discount and refund report once, because a pattern by shift usually shows quickly.

workzap_build.text: a daily discount, void and refund report by branch, shift and role, with an alert when any branch crosses the limit you set.

problems.ask_first: Who can apply a discount or refund on the POS today?
problems.free_stops: The thresholds and approval rules per role are set in the solution document.

problems.words: Five tablets for five apps, and app payouts never match the POS
quick_ideas: Match one app's payout against POS orders once, so you know whether the gap is missed orders or deductions
Put all tablets in one spot with one person watching them at peak.

workzap_build.text: and cash_reconciliation — all app orders on one screen beside POS sales, and each app's payout reconciled every day with commission, refunds and missed orders shown.

problems.ask_first: Which app's payout confuses you most?
problems.free_stops: Which apps connect and how the reconciliation rules work goes in the solution document.

problems.words: Riders take longer routes, ask for more fuel money, and food arrives cold
quick_ideas: Note time out and back for each trip for a few days, so fuel claims can be compared with real trips
Agree a fuel allowance by area instead of by request, so there's less to argue about.

workzap_build.text: a rider log of trips, areas, delivery times and fuel claims by rider label, summarised daily per branch.

problems.ask_first: Are riders your own, the app's, or both?
problems.free_stops: The allowance rules and how trips are checked against claims stay for the solution document.

problems.words: Crew turnover is constant, and overtime claims don't match the clock-in
quick_ideas: Pair each new cashier with one experienced person for their first shifts, because a rough first week is when people quit
Have the shift manager approve overtime the same night, while it's still fresh.

workzap_build.text: crew rota and clock-in on phone, with overtime summarised automatically per branch for approval.

problems.ask_first: Which shift is hardest to staff?
problems.free_stops: The onboarding plan and overtime approval rules are in the solution document.

problems.words: Head office reports come a week late and in different Excel formats from each branch
quick_ideas: Ask every branch for one daily number by morning, so you're not waiting a week
Pick the one number you'll check every day, because too many numbers means none get read.

workzap_build.text: a short morning read on WhatsApp of every branch's sales, channel mix, discounts and stock flags, with the one branch to look at.

problems.ask_first: What one number would you check every morning?
problems.free_stops: What goes into the morning read and how branch data is pulled is in the solution document.

problems.words: Our LTO launch flopped and loyalty stamps on paper cards get lost
quick_ideas: Note the promoted item's sales before, during and after the next LTO, so you can judge it fairly
Ask regulars if they'd like a phone-number visit count, with their permission, instead of paper stamps.

workzap_build.text: and loyalty_repeat — codes showing which channel brought each order, an LTO tracker measured automatically, and phone-number loyalty for opted-in customers.

problems.ask_first: How do you judge whether a deal or LTO worked today?
problems.free_stops: The code set-up per channel and the loyalty rules are kept for the solution document.

never_say: Advice on franchise agreements, royalties or disputes with franchisees — that is for their lawyer. Anything on food-safety certification, oil-disposal rules or allergens — refer to the authority or a qualified consultant. Tracking crew or riders' personal phones without their knowledge. Help suppressing sales from royalty reports or tax. Any promise that ticket times, sales or margins will improve by a set amount.

sample_reply.person: We have nine branches, four franchised. I need a solution I never know what the franchise ones are really selling, and two use their own POS.
sample_reply.pi: Yes, you can get proper visibility, and the first steps can start this week. 1 Ask every franchisee for the same few numbers on a fixed day, so their reports can at least be compared. 2 Visit one franchised branch at peak and compare what you see with what they send. Workzap can do this automatically for you, pulling sales from every outlet, including the two on their own POS, into one dashboard by hour and channel, with a short morning read on WhatsApp. Shall I get a solution document and quote prepared for you? You're welcome to say no.
